data.title: Cuba wins UN vote against US embargo but support dips
data.description: UNITED NATIONS - The UN General Assembly on Wednesday adopted a new resolution calling for an end to the US embargo against Cuba, although support for the communist-ruled island fell to its lowest level in three decades.

data.title: Nurses oppose govt volunteer plans
data.description: The Nurses Association of Thailand has opposed the government's Community Nursing Volunteer initiative, urging authorities to review the policy and promote oversight to protect patient safety and healthcare standards.

data.title: Mister Donut & After You Partner Again After Selling 2 Million Donuts
data.description: Mister Donut, operated by Central Restaurants Group Co., Ltd. (CRG), is continuing its brand collaboration strategy by partnering with After You for “Mister Donut x After You Season 2”. Following the success of their first collaboration, which sold nearly 2 million donuts and generated strong buzz across social media, the two brands are introducing five new creations under the “Japanese Autumn” concept. Inspired by Japan’s autumn season, the collection combines distinctive flavours and textures, highlighted by a specially developed mochi donut recipe created exclusively for this campaign. The collaboration aims to introduce innovative dessert experiences, attract new consumer segments, and strengthen the brands’ market presence.

data.title: PM rejects solar bias claims
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul on Wednesday criticised media reports linking major corporations, including Sino-Thai Engineering and Construction Plc, to the government's household solar rooftop scheme, rejecting claims that the project was designed to favour large businesses.

data.title: Space cooperation scheme secures regional backing
data.description: Thailand has secured regional backing for a space cooperation framework through 2030, with 62 members and associate members of the United Nations' Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (Escap) adopting the Bangkok Declaration by consensus.

data.title: Nationality fraud crackdown boosted
data.description: The Interior Ministry has vowed to intensify its crackdown on nationality fraud, illegal foreign nominee businesses and corrupt officials, while stepping up investigations through digital technology and closer inter-agency cooperation.

data.title: Chadchart rejects claims of relief rift
data.description: Bangkok governor Chadchart Sittipunt has denied a conflict with the government over flood relief funding, saying budget procedures and regulations govern how additional assistance can be provided.

data.title: The draw of a spooky night out
data.description: As Halloween approaches, Khao San Road is getting into the spirit of the season, with bars, restaurants and shops transforming their premises into spooky attractions in a bid to draw crowds and boost spending.

data.title: PP backs groups opposing fund law changes
data.description: Opposition People's Party (PP) leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut said he shared the concerns of civil society groups opposing amendments to four laws that would change the funding arrangements for public bodies.

data.title: Aluminium in river 'poses low risk' to environment
data.description: The Department of Pollution Control says aluminium detected in the Prachin Buri River is unlikely to pose a significant risk to health or the environment, as the water's pH level may cause the metal to settle in river sediments.

data.title: Tax revenue shake-up draws fire
data.description: Four proposed legal amendments could put about 14 billion baht a year in funding for health promotion, public broadcasting, elderly welfare and sports development at the government's discretion, prompting public opposition to plans to end their automatic share of alcohol and tobacco tax revenue.

data.title: Thailand eyes regional space hub plan
data.description: Her Royal Highness Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn presided over the opening of Thailand Space Expo 2026 at ICONSIAM in Bangkok on Wednesday, highlighting Thailand's growing role in the global space industry and its ambition to become a regional hub for space technology and innovation.

data.title: No-confidence debate set for Dec 7-11
data.description: A three-party coordination committee yesterday agreed to hold the no-confidence debate against the government on Dec 7-11, allocating 51 hours to the opposition, 17 hours to the cabinet and government, and four hours to the House speaker.

data.title: Cuba wins UN vote against US embargo with weakest backing in 30 years
data.description: UNITED NATIONS (UNITED STATES) - The UN General Assembly on Wednesday adopted a new resolution calling for an end to the US embargo against Cuba, although support for the communist-ruled island fell to its lowest level in three decades.

data.title: Putin hails Elon Musk as 'truly a genius'
data.description: MOSCOW - US tech tycoon Elon Musk is "truly a genius" for deploying thousands of satellites into orbit, President Vladimir Putin said Wednesday, as Moscow seeks to develop its own satellite internet network.

data.title: Italian PM slams 'shameful' release of alleged protest organiser
data.description: ROME - Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Wednesday slammed a "shameful" decision by a judge dismissing accusations against a campaigner arrested on terrorism charges for allegedly seeking to organise violent protests.

data.title: Bolsonaro's escape to the US: How it happened
data.description: SAO PAULO - Flavio Bolsonaro's clandestine escape to the United States bewildered Brazil and triggered a frantic search for his whereabouts.

data.title: World Bank warns of worsening food insecurity as commodity prices soar
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The World Bank on Wednesday warned that global commodity prices were set to increase by 23 percent by the end of 2026, with energy prices at four-year highs due to the war on Iran and food prices driven up by global conflicts and El Nino.

data.title: Clean-up starts as Serbian students movement prepares to govern
data.description: BELGRADE - Belgrade residents on Wednesday washed away politically charged graffiti that had stained city walls over months of protests, as Serbia's student-led movement prepared to govern after its seismic election victory.

data.title: High-speed train crash in Spain kills at least 64
data.description: URDA, Spain - A high-speed train collision south of Madrid killed 64 people and injured scores more on Wednesday, with the toll likely to rise, authorities said after one of Europe’s deadliest such disasters this century.

data.title: Bolsonaro flees Brazil for US after election defeat
data.description: OPA-LOCKA, Florida - Brazil’s defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro arrived in Florida by private plane on Wednesday, after defying a court order that banned him from leaving his country.

data.title: Russell Brand gives evidence in rape trial
data.description: LONDON - British comedian and actor Russell Brand told his rape trial on Wednesday that he believed consent was “fundamental” to sexual relations, as he gave evidence for the first time.

data.title: Russia woos African leaders at Moscow summit
data.description: MOSCOW - A summit with nearly two dozen African leaders opened in Moscow Wednesday, with the Kremlin describing their countries as “natural allies” against the West.

data.title: Climate talks ‘a bunch of baloney and BS’, says Panama
data.description: YEREVAN, Armenia - Despite campaigning to host the next COP nature summit, Panama’s Environment Minister Juan Carlos Navarro has a blunt view of the UN-led negotiations he says are little more than “hypocrisy contests”.

data.title: Turkey brokers Libyan reunification talks
data.description: ISTANBUL - Turkey hosted talks between Libya’s eastern and western administrations last week with an ultimate goal of reunifying them, but no agreement has emerged, a senior Turkish official familiar with the talks told AFP Wednesday.

data.title: High-speed train crash in Spain kills at least 30
data.description: URDA, Spain - A collision between two high-speed trains south of Madrid killed 30 people on Wednesday and the toll could rise, regional authorities said in Spain’s second such disaster this year.

data.title: Thai housing groups seek tax relief as loan rejections may hit 50%
data.description: Proposals include a 200,000-baht homebuyer tax deduction cap and lower taxes on unsold homes ahead of the October 29–November 1 property show.

data.title: Fake paternity filings prompt hospital probe
data.description: Public Health Minister Pattana Promphat has ordered a thorough investigation into private hospitals believed linked to fake paternity registrations, following reports that the scheme might date back more than two decades.

data.title: Public input sought in southern peace talks
data.description: Thailand plans to expand peace talks in the deep South beyond the Barisan Revolusi Nasional (BRN), with greater public participation seen as essential to achieving a lasting solution, Deputy Prime Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said on Wednesday.

data.title: Israel’s low-key president holds keys to next government
data.description: JERUSALEM - Israeli President Isaac Herzog is known for his unassuming and mild manner, but all eyes will soon be on him as he decides who to task with forming the next coalition government.

data.title: Phuket mayor blames mudslide on hill encroachment
data.description: PHUKET - The mayor of Patong municipality has blamed encroachment on nearby hills by property developers for causing the huge mudslides that struck the area on Monday.
